answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a anchor as the anchor of the cost.
